Summarise Gorilla data

Source: R/summary.R
summary.gorilla_data.Rd

Describes each task and questionnaire in one row, as a first check of the data after reading them.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gorilla_data'
summary(object, fast = 200, slow = 10000, ...)

Arguments

object

A gorilla_data object from read_gorilla().

fast, slow

Reaction times in milliseconds below fast or above slow are counted as fast or slow responses.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class gorilla_summary: a list with two tibbles.

tasks

One row per task: builder, number of participants, number of responses per participant (minimum, median and maximum), the proportion of responses marked as correct, the median reaction time, the proportions of fast and slow responses and the median time participants spent on the task, in minutes. The proportion correct only means something for tasks with scoring set up in 'Gorilla': components without scoring mark every response as correct, and rating scales count a response as correct only if it matches the answer column of the spreadsheet.

questionnaires

One row per questionnaire: number of participants, number of items and the proportion of items left unanswered.

See also

gorilla_checks() to list participants who may need a closer look.

Examples

g <- read_gorilla(gorilla_example(), quiet = TRUE)
summary(g)
#> 6 participants (complete: 5, live: 1)
#> 
#> Tasks
#>         task_name        builder participants responses_min responses_median
#>  Lexical decision Task Builder 2            6             7               16
#>   Rhyme judgement Task Builder 1            5             8                8
#>  responses_max correct rt_median fast slow minutes
#>             16   0.943     673.1    0    0     0.4
#>              8   0.950     910.1    0    0     0.4
#> 
#> Questionnaires
#>   task_name participants items unanswered
#>  Background            6     7          0
#>     Consent            6     2          0
summary(g)$tasks
#> # A tibble: 2 × 11
#>   task_name    builder participants responses_min responses_median responses_max
#>   <chr>        <chr>          <int>         <int>            <dbl>         <int>
#> 1 Lexical dec… Task B…            6             7               16            16
#> 2 Rhyme judge… Task B…            5             8                8             8
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: correct <dbl>, rt_median <dbl>, fast <dbl>, slow <dbl>,
#> #   minutes <dbl>
